studies.title: How Do You Identify a Good Manager?
studies.authors: Ben Weidmann; Joseph Vecci; Farah Said; Sonia Bhalotra; Achyuta Adhvaryu; Anant Nyshadham; Jorge Tamayo; David Deming
studies.design: Randomized manager/team assignments and selection-rule experiment
studies.finding: Manager contributions mattered substantially; self-selected managers performed worse than randomly selected managers.
studies.identification_risk: Controlled task effects do not establish the return to a manager-selection policy in an operating firm.
studies.depth: Publisher abstract and experimental design discussion
studies.date_basis: Publisher-deposited first-online date; day absent where unavailable.
studies.citation: Ben Weidmann; Joseph Vecci; Farah Said; Sonia Bhalotra; Achyuta Adhvaryu; Anant Nyshadham; Jorge Tamayo; David Deming (2026). How Do You Identify a Good Manager? Quarterly Journal of Economics. https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjag004
studies.direction_rationale: Coded worsened for the practice of letting managers self-select: they performed worse than randomly selected managers.
